what: THE ONE SOURCE REGISTRY. Every source any lane reads is a row here, under one canonical id with one durable cursor, and is ACTIVE only when a cell of it was EVALUATED by the gauntlet within 30 days. Built by libs/mining/acquirer.load_roster from libs/mining/sources.yaml and every table its external_rosters name; published hourly by the global_mining leg.
how_to_register: Write your rows to a file under desks/mt5/data/source_rosters/ (*.json, *.jsonl or *.yaml; a document's 'sources', 'rows' or 'grounds' list, or a bare list). It is picked up on the next hourly pass; no code change.
Or, for a table that already exists elsewhere, add one entry to external_rosters in libs/mining/sources.yaml: {path: <glob>, rows: <list key>, id_style: <prefix for unnamed rows>, defaults: {...}}.
fetcher: owned means YOUR organ fetches and consumes the source; the mining pipeline never fetches it twice, it only registers and accounts it.

The first definition of an id wins, so no lane can redefine another's row. A row from another roster naming the same page (canonical_url) AND the same thing (slug of name) becomes an alias of the first; same page, different thing stays two sources linked by shares_page.

roster_row.id: string, required unless the entry declares id_style; alias: source_id. Stable forever: it keys the cursor.
roster_row.name: string, human label
roster_row.url: string; aliases rss, link, page1, or the first of urls/roots/feeds/alt. The cross-roster join key (canonical_url: host + path + sorted query, lower-case).
roster_row.fetcher: owned | html_listing | rss | reddit_json | github_search | telegram_preview | json_api | search_route | page_snapshot | external_feed
roster_row.owner: string, the lane accountable for it (e.g. breadth/free_stack, country_pack/jp)
roster_row.consumer: repo path of the organ that consumes it
roster_row.uses: list of direct_cells | indirect_cells | allocation_intel; defaults by kind
roster_row.region: string, country or cluster code; default global
roster_row.auth: none | optional | key | login; auth_env names the env var holding the key (never the key)
roster_row.cadence: cadence_minutes | cadence_s | cadence_hours | cadence (hourly, daily, weekly, 6h, 2d)
roster_row.config: fetcher-specific; url/urls/listing/feeds/queries/subs/channels/pages/paths/item_regex may sit on the row

registry_row.cold_reason: '' | 'serves no use' | 'no cell EVALUATED in 30 days'
registry_row.evaluated_via: {mining: mining-pipeline cells EVALUATED in 30 days, docket: docket cells judged in 30 days attributed to this source through miner_candidates.json (source_url longest path prefix on the same host, a host with one registered source, or the seat named in source) x judged_cells}
registry_row.origin: the roster file the row came from
registry_row.aliases: ids other rosters gave this same source
registry_row.shares_page: ids of distinct sources declared on the same page
registry_row.last_outcome: the pipeline's last fetch outcome for sources it fetches; NEVER_RUN for owned rows
registry_row.records_total: records stored in the PIT store
registry_row.cursor: desks/mt5/data/mining/cursors/<id>.json on the box: {registered: {canonical_id, origin, owner, url_key, aliases, shares_page, first_seen}, ...fetch state}

where.summary_committed: desks/mt5/data/mining_digest.json -> registry (per owner: sources, active, cold by reason; the attribution basis) and sources (ACTIVE rows and the pipeline's own fetchers)

limits: Attribution reads the compiler's CURRENT docket snapshot, so a judged candidate that has since left it is not credited (an undercount, never an overcount). A lane whose cells never reach the compiler (a conditioner series, an allocator input) stays COLD until its cells reach the gauntlet: that is the rule, not a defect of it.
